# Retirement Withdrawal Calculator
# https://github.com/YidiDev/retirement-planning-calculator

> This is an open-source retirement withdrawal calculator that stress-tests
> flexible withdrawal strategies against 150+ years of real U.S. market history.

## What this tool does

This calculator helps people plan retirement withdrawals by replaying a
configurable strategy through every starting month in U.S. market history
since 1871. The user sets:

- Retirement savings (nest egg)
- Retirement length (5-60 years)
- Goal (preserve capital, spend it down, or custom retention %)
- Portfolio allocation (stocks, bonds, gold, or custom mix)
- Withdrawal floor (minimum monthly income)
- Withdrawal cap (maximum monthly income)

The calculator optimizes a "sensitivity" parameter that determines how
strongly withdrawals react to recent market performance, then reports:

- Median safe monthly withdrawal
- Historical success rate (% of periods that met the goal)
- Income charts across all historical periods
- Capital preservation chart
- Spotlight on individual retirement periods (worst, best, typical)
- Full table of every simulated retirement

## How the simulation works

Each month, the retiree withdraws a percentage of their current portfolio.
That percentage flexes between a floor and a cap based on recent market
returns. The formula:

    raw_rate = sensitivity × lookback_return × 12 / lookback_months
    withdrawal_rate = clamp(raw_rate, floor, cap)

The withdrawal is the maximum of:
- The percentage-based amount (rate × portfolio / 12)
- The fixed dollar floor (if set)

And the minimum of:
- The withdrawal amount
- The fixed dollar cap (if set)

## Data sources

- U.S. Equity: S&P 500 total return (monthly, 1871-2023) from Robert Shiller
- Treasury Bonds: 10-year constant maturity return (monthly, 1871-2023)
- Gold: monthly prices (free-market era, 1968-2023)
- Inflation: CPI-U for real-return calculations

The simulation maps all user-selected assets into three "sleeves":
equity, bonds, and gold. The portfolio allocation determines the
blend of these three return streams.

## Technical architecture

- Frontend: Alpine.js for reactivity, Chart.js for charts
- Styling: Tailwind CSS v4 with custom warm paper design
- Computation: Web Worker running grid search + refinement optimizer
- Build: Vite (dev dependency only, not in production output)
- Data pipeline: Python scripts for Yahoo Finance / FRED collection

## Limitations

- Historical backtest only — does not predict future performance
- Taxes, fees, and fund expenses are not modeled
- Assumes monthly rebalancing to target allocation
- Gold data limited to 1968+ (pre-1968 was gold standard)
- Not financial advice — consult a qualified advisor
